movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items', column FY24 (Sept 24) -> column FY25 (Sept 25)
headline: Westpac's cash earnings (net profit excluding Notable Items) decreased by 2% to $6,972 million in FY25 from $7,113 million in FY24. The decline was driven by higher operating expenses, partially offset by increased net interest income and lower credit impairment charges. Statutory profit also fell slightly to $6,933 million (from $6,990 million), with notable items reducing statutory profit by $56 million compared to a $123 million reduction in FY24.

drivers.narrative: NII increased by 3% to $19,473 million (from $18,916 million). This reflects volume growth of 4% in average loans ($764.4bn vs $732.7bn), which was partially offset by a 1 bps compression in core NIM (1.81% vs 1.82%). Treasury & Markets NII remained stable at $1,039 million.
Other operating income rose by 5% to $2,991 million (from $2,847 million). Net fees contributed positively, increasing 4% to $1,732 million. Trading income and other income also saw modest increases.

Total operating expenses increased by 9% to $11,916 million (from $10,944 million). This includes a $273 million restructuring charge ('Fit for Growth') in H2. Underlying expenses grew 6%, driven by a 7% rise in staff costs ($6,326 million) and a 13% increase in technology expenses ($3,136 million), partially offset by lower occupancy costs.

The bank incurred a $273 million restructuring charge in H2 FY25 as part of its 'Fit for Growth' program. In FY24, there were no comparable restructuring charges reported in the notable items table. This is a specific component of the total operating expense movement.

Credit impairment charges decreased by 21% to $424 million (from $537 million). Lower provisions improved cash earnings relative to the prior year, reflecting stable credit quality despite higher expense levels.

Tax expense decreased slightly by 1% to $3,135 million (from $3,169 million). The effective tax rate remained broadly consistent, resulting in a small positive contribution to the after-tax earnings delta.

notable_items: Restructuring costs: $273 million in FY25 (H2 only); $0 in FY24.
limitations: The residual of -$7 million likely stems from rounding differences between the headline cash earnings delta (-$141m) and the sum of the quantified drivers (-$134m). Specifically, the NII and Other Income figures used are 'ex-notables', while the Tax figure is statutory; reconciling these bases precisely requires the full statutory-to-cash bridge which is not fully itemized in the provided text for the comparative period.

The 'Notable Items' driver is treated separately from Operating Expenses per instructions, but it is embedded within the Total Operating Expenses line item in the primary P&L table. The narrative separates them for clarity.

Capped at 80: nii +557 $m, other_operating_income +157 $m, credit_impairment_charge +113 $m, tax_and_other +24 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
Failed check: drivers_reconcile (drivers -394.0 + residual -7.0 != delta -141.0, tol 1.0)
